title: Should You Buy Sony?

Sony Corp. ( NYSE:SNE ) had an impressive up run in 2017 as the stock surged more than 60%. Also, the stock is off a good start heading into 2018, escalating more than 12% year to date. The stock currently trades at its multi-year high and looks like it will continue hitting new highs in the years ahead. 
Sony reported robust third-quarter results on Feb. 2. For the quarter, the company posted record earnings per share of $2.03 (¥229) per share, representing growth of 1400% compared to the same quarter a year ago. 
Its revenue came in at $23.6 billion (¥2,672.2 billion) signifying a surge of 11.5% year-over-year. The revenue growth was primarily driven by robust growth in game and network services (G&NS) as well as home entertainment and sound (HE&S) segments. The effect of foreign currency translation also compelled top-line growth. 
Throughout the past 12 months, the continuously growing sales of PlayStation 4 have boosted Sony’s top line. According to the latest report from VGChartz, Sony has sold a total of 75.3 million units of PlayStation 4 (PS4) since its launch. That figure is substantially higher than the sales of Microsoft’s ( NASDAQ:MSFT ) XBOX ONE and Nintendo’s ( NTDOY ) Switch. Peter Lynch Chart of SNE 
Source: VGChartz 
The company’s sizeable PS4 user base helps to produce substantial profits from software sales, in particular, high-end digital transactions as well as subscriptions. Sony’s PlayStation 4 is now five years old, but the sales of PS4 are still growing at a healthy rate. 
Keeping in mind Sony’s existing base of over 75 million PS4 users, the company looks well-positioned to benefit from virtual reality (VR). The company has sold over 2 million VR headsets, and that makes it the leader of VR market. 
Furthermore, the outstanding performance of its semiconductor business is proving to be a great profit churner. During the last quarter, the company’s semiconductor business generated the highest operating margin of 24%. 
The company’s semiconductor business will continue producing strong results in the upcoming years as it supplies premium sensors to numerous high-end smartphone makers and is not only reliant on Apple’s (AAPL) iPhone models. 
Apart from this, several measures adopted by the company including a reduction in advertisement expenses, cost-reduction initiatives as well as declining exposure in low-profit areas will help it to grow well in the forthcoming years. 
At present, Sony’s mobile communications business accounted for the worst performing business segment as it has lost its charm it had several years ago. However, the company is aggressively trying to make a comeback in the smartphone industry. The company is about to launch new Xperia X72 featuring HD playback quality comparable to its Bravia TVs. It also has a rumble feature adapted from its game machine. 
For the current quarter, Sony expects to earn $4.5 billion, almost 26% more profit than it previously had predicted. 
Summing up 
Although Sony’s stock price has appreciated over 100% throughout the past two years, it still has legs to run higher. The company has faced several problems regarding profitability in the past, but now it consists of a stable and diverse business with $23.6 billion revenue and $3.1 billion operating income. 
On the other hand, the stock currently trades at a trailing 12-month price-earnings (PE) ratio of just 13.16, significantly less than the industry’s average of 25, suggesting it is undervalued. Also, it offers a trailing 12-month dividend yield of 0.44% with a payout ratio below 50%. Though current dividend yield is not attractive, it has plenty of room to increase its dividend in the years ahead. 
As a result, shareholders should consider buying the stock at a current market price, as its future looks strong.
